findings.description: 'Systematic mapping' claim without defined inclusion criteria. The 17 principles derive from author selection, not a comprehensive literature review with stated search strategy or inclusion/exclusion criteria. 'Systematic' implies exhaustiveness the methodology section does not establish.
findings.suggestion: Replace 'systematic mapping' with 'structured mapping' or 'principled mapping', or add a sentence establishing the selection criteria (e.g., 'We surveyed CPG literature reviews by Grillner (1985, 2006) and Marder (2012) and selected principles with plausible software analogues').
findings.context: We borrowed this design for AI cognitive architecture. Not as metaphor, but as a systematic mapping: 17 CPG principles from the neuroscience literature

findings.description: Governance collapse claim lacks empirical evidence. 'AI governance systems that only add rules and never remove them eventually collapse under their own weight' presents a causal prediction as established fact. No AI governance system has operated long enough to demonstrate this failure mode empirically.
findings.suggestion: Hedge the claim: 'AI governance systems that only add rules risk accumulating contradictions over time' or cite analogous evidence from regulatory domain (e.g., tax code complexity, building code accumulation).
findings.context: AI governance systems that only add rules and never remove them eventually collapse under their own weight

findings.description: Central concepts in this post lack glossary coverage. 'Central Pattern Generator' (CPG), 'crystallization', 'cognitive architecture', and 'adaptive forgetting' appear as key terms throughout the post but have no entries in src/data/glossary.ts. The glossary covers 49 terms across 8 categories; these 4 terms fit the 'architecture' or 'methodology' categories.
findings.suggestion: Add glossary entries for at minimum 'CPG' and 'crystallization' (the two most frequently used terms). Category: 'architecture'. These terms appear in blog content and may appear in future site pages.
findings.context: glossary.ts contains 49 terms; none cover CPG, crystallization, cognitive architecture, or adaptive forgetting

findings.description: Zero internal cross-links in a 253-line post. The post discusses concepts (four scarcities, safety mechanisms, governance frameworks) that connect to existing site pages (/connection/ai/higher-order-effects, /glossary, /connection/ai/differential-diagnosis) but contains no internal links. Reduces discoverability and site cohesion.
findings.suggestion: Add 2-3 strategic cross-links where concepts overlap with existing site content. Candidates: 'four new bottlenecks' (line 60, link to /connection/ai/higher-order-effects), 'governance mechanisms' (line 168, link to /connection/ai/ratification-counterfactual), glossary terms on first use.
findings.context: 253-line blog post with 0 internal links; related site pages exist for four-scarcities, governance, and differential-diagnosis

findings.description: Published post carries reviewStatus: 'pending'. The post has draft: false and publishedDate: 2026-03-15 (9 days ago) but reviewStatus remains 'pending'. This suggests the post reached publication without completing its review cycle, or the review cycle completed without updating the frontmatter field.
findings.suggestion: Update reviewStatus to 'reviewed' if review occurred, or conduct review and update. If the field tracks peer review specifically, flag this as a process gap in the blog publishing workflow.

findings.description: 'Hard-coding every behavior produces brittle systems' stated as universal fact without citation. Software engineering literature broadly supports this claim, but the post presents it without attribution.
findings.suggestion: Add a parenthetical citation or qualify: 'Hard-coding every behavior tends to produce brittle systems (a well-documented pattern in software engineering)' or cite a specific source.
findings.context: Hard-coding every behavior produces brittle systems. Leaving everything to runtime deliberation wastes processing capacity

epistemic_flags: Fair-witness findings apply the psychology-agent's editorial standards, which may differ from the unratified site's intended register for blog content
Vocabulary findings assume the glossary should cover blog-introduced terms; the site may intentionally limit glossary scope to core analytical content
